scope: PR421 finite verification reproduction and adversarial runtime validation only
hypothesis: The three frozen verification programs independently validate their stated finite certificate and reject relevant corruptions; neither replay nor finite certificates alone establish global geometry.
success_criteria: Every receipt file byte count and SHA-256 matches the copied frozen snapshot and git object at the pinned head.
All source programs and their source/document inputs are read completely before execution; historical audit verdicts are deferred until this criteria seal exists.

Each program is replayed in private clean fixtures under normal Python and -O with stale generated outputs removed and actual argv, interpreter, version, duration, stdout/stderr, exit, and output hashes recorded.
Validate actual runtime checks, exact bounds and artifact provenance; success strings without executing checks do not count as validation.

Separate meaningful corruptions cover Q link fullness, cube corner or face incidence, stable-letter signs, and proof input bytes; all normal or repaired claimed validations must reject such controls for the intended reason.
Any proposed repair must remain a separate explicit-check overlay with frozen originals unmodified, mutation provenance and fresh replays; report the original failure independently of repair.
Evidence and final verdict clearly distinguish finite combinatorial computations, forward target-word checks, proof input identity, and unverified global semantic implications.
boundary_cases: stale outputs can impersonate completed validation
source byte mutations outside algebra checks
each of 16 cube corners; face attachment compatibility
finite forward relators do not alone prove reverse presentation equivalence
